response.message:
We're drawing a signed-in chat assistant on AWS. The browser goes through CloudFront, Cognito and API Gateway to a Lambda chat handler. That handler keeps each user's conversation in DynamoDB, sends Bedrock only a limited recent window of the chat, and passes escalations to an SQS queue for a person to review. It takes no external actions.

The first local test can check sign-in claims, saving each user's conversation separately, the window limit and escalation routing, using scripted model replies. That shows the plumbing works, but it says nothing about answer quality. Real model checks need approved model access in a chosen account and region, and none of that is confirmed yet. Also, our generator doesn't cover this chat Lambda or the escalation queue yet, so both still need engineering work.

When the assistant escalates, who should pick it up: a support person working from a queue, or an existing ticketing tool?

proposal.title: Authenticated conversational assistant on AWS (first sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: a signed-in web chat for synthetic users, with conversation history kept separately for each user, a limited context window, Bedrock model calls and escalation to a person. No external actions. Assumptions: the region, account, model ID and who handles escalations are not decided yet. The chat Lambda, conversation table and escalation queue have no typed generator yet and still need engineering work. Nothing here is verified or deployed.

data.label: Synthetic user (browser)
data.description: Test user's browser. A client reference, not a provisioned service.

data.label: Chat web app
data.description: Serves the chat interface from private S3 assets that CloudFront owns. Signs users in with authorization code + PKCE and sends their token with each chat request.

data.label: User sign-in
data.description: User pool for synthetic users created by an admin. MFA is proposed. Issues the JWTs that the API checks.

data.label: Chat API
data.description: HTTP API with a JWT authorizer. Rejects requests without a valid token and applies throttling.

data.label: Chat orchestrator
data.description: Takes the user ID from the verified token, loads that user's conversation, trims context to a limited window (the last N turns or a token budget), calls the model, saves the turn and returns the reply. Decides when to escalate. Has no tools or external actions. Owns its execution role, logs, version and alias.

data.label: Conversation state
data.description: Partitioned by user ID and keyed by conversation and turn. A TTL removes old conversations. Access is scoped to the calling user's partition.

data.label: Model runtime
data.description: A direct foundation model is called through the Converse API. The model ID, access, quotas and region availability are not yet verified.

data.label: Escalation queue
data.description: Holds escalated conversations, with their reason and a conversation reference, for human review. A dead-letter queue and alarm are still to be designed.

data.label: Support reviewer
data.description: The person who picks up escalations. How they work (queue console or ticketing tool) is still open.

data.label: Logs & metrics
data.description: Logs, latency, error and escalation metrics for the API and Lambda. Retention is to be agreed.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without this, one user could see another user's chat history.
requirementDrafts.basis: Brief: 'authenticated conversational assistant' with 'per-user conversation state'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: each authenticated user can read and continue only their own conversations; requests without a valid token are rejected.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Unlimited history makes cost and latency grow and can push past the model's limits.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: the assistant sends the model only a limited window of recent conversation, with input and output limits set as configuration.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Gives users a safe handoff while keeping the first test free of side effects.
requirementDrafts.basis: Brief: 'an escalation path. No external actions in this first test.'
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: when the assistant cannot help or the user asks for a person, it records an escalation for human review and takes no other external action.

response.message:
Good news first: the check found no failed tests, so nothing in the design is broken. It's blocked because our generator doesn't have code yet for the chat Lambda, conversation store, escalation queue, or the CloudFront, Cognito and API Gateway setup for this chat use case. Some of those look like the RAG web contracts, but those contracts are only for keyword search over documents. Moving this design onto them would quietly turn the assistant into something else, so I've left the diagram as it is.

The fix belongs in the product. It needs a typed conversational-assistant contract, and a test case already exists: this revision 2 artifact (digest b63a8e00…). That contract would give us a user-scoped DynamoDB table, a limited context window and an SQS escalation queue with a dead-letter queue. Once that's built, we export and run the local test again.

To shape that contract: when the assistant escalates, should a support person work straight from the queue, or should escalations go into an existing ticketing tool?
